subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Poetry written without a regular rhyme scheme or fixed metre is called...
questions.explain: Free verse abandons regular rhyme and metre, allowing rhythm to follow natural speech and meaning.

questions.q: Who does the pig Squealer represent as he spreads Napoleon's propaganda in Animal Farm?
questions.explain: Squealer is an allegory for Stalinist propaganda that manipulates the other animals.

questions.q: Animal Farm is an allegory for which historical event?
questions.explain: Orwell's fable allegorises the Russian Revolution and the rise of Stalinist tyranny.

questions.q: How might 'sibilance' (repeated 's' sounds) be analysed in a poem?
options: It can create a soft, hissing or soothing sound that shapes mood
It tells us the poet's age
It proves the poem is a sonnet
questions.explain: Sibilance creates an audible texture, soft and hushed or sinister and snake-like, that an analyst connects to mood.

questions.q: When analysing an UNSEEN poem, the best first step is to...
options: Read for overall meaning and identify the main idea or feeling
questions.explain: Grasping the poem's central idea or feeling first gives you a framework to then analyse how methods create it.

questions.q: When a poet ends a poem on a single short line after longer ones, this can...
options: Prove the poem is free verse
Create emphasis, abruptness or a sense of finality
Mean the poet ran out of ideas
questions.explain: An isolated short final line draws the eye and ear, lending weight, shock or closure to the poem's ending.

questions.q: What major building project causes hardship and dispute among the animals?
questions.explain: The windmill, repeatedly built and destroyed, becomes a symbol of the animals' exploited labour.

questions.q: What is Boxer the carthorse's personal motto?
questions.explain: Boxer's maxim "I will work harder" shows his loyalty and tireless effort.

questions.q: A poem of fourteen lines, often in iambic pentameter with a turn in argument, is most likely a...
questions.explain: The fourteen-line form with a volta is the defining feature of a sonnet.

questions.q: When poets present 'love and relationships', the tone may be...
options: Varied: tender, bitter, possessive or disillusioned depending on the poem
questions.explain: Relationship poems span many tones, so identifying the specific attitude to love is key to analysis.

questions.q: A useful comparative connective to show contrast between two poems is...
questions.explain: Connectives like 'whereas', 'in contrast' and 'similarly' signal genuine comparison between the two poems' methods.

questions.q: A poem spoken in the voice of a single fictional speaker, revealing their character to a silent listener, is a...
questions.explain: A dramatic monologue uses one speaker's voice to expose their personality, often unintentionally, to an implied listener.

questions.q: How does Napoleon justify taking the milk and apples only for the pigs?
options: The pigs won them in a vote
Squealer claims the pigs need them as brainworkers to run the farm
questions.explain: Squealer argues the pigs require the milk and apples for their brain-work, an early sign of their privilege and corruption.

questions.q: What happens to the windmill the first time the animals complete it?
options: It is destroyed in a storm, which Napoleon blames on Snowball
questions.explain: A storm topples the windmill, and Napoleon scapegoats the exiled Snowball to deflect blame.

questions.q: What does the cynical donkey Benjamin represent in the novella?
options: Weary scepticism and those who see corruption but do nothing
questions.explain: Benjamin distrusts the pigs and foresees disaster but stays passive, representing cynical inaction in the face of tyranny.

questions.q: How do poets commonly present the theme of 'power'?
options: By showing it as permanent and unchallengeable always
Often by exposing how power is temporary, corrupting or undermined by time/nature
questions.explain: Many power poems explore its fragility, arrogance or eventual decay, contrasting human power with time or nature.

questions.q: Which Soviet leaders are Napoleon and Snowball generally taken to represent?
questions.explain: Napoleon represents Stalin and Snowball represents Trotsky, who was driven into exile.

questions.q: In Animal Farm, who is the farmer the animals overthrow in the Rebellion?
questions.explain: The animals rebel against the neglectful, drunken Mr Jones and drive him from the farm.

questions.q: What is the novella's central message about power?
options: Power corrupts, and idealistic revolutions can be betrayed
Animals make better leaders than humans
questions.explain: Orwell shows how the pigs' growing corruption betrays the revolution, illustrating that power corrupts.

questions.q: Repetition of a key word or phrase in a poem usually serves to...
options: Signal the end of the anthology
Emphasise an idea or emotion and create rhythm or insistence
questions.explain: Repetition foregrounds an idea, building emphasis, rhythm or a sense of obsession depending on context.

questions.q: In Animal Farm, the commandment 'All animals are equal' is finally altered to add which words?
options: 'but some are more equal than others'
questions.explain: The amended commandment exposes the pigs' hypocrisy and the betrayal of equality.

questions.q: Imagery that appeals to the senses (sight, sound, touch) is used by poets mainly to...
options: Make experiences vivid and draw the reader into the poem's world
questions.explain: Sensory imagery immerses the reader, making emotions and scenes feel concrete and immediate.
